title: Evidence lifecycle + fast-path onboarding PRD (draft)
content:
Purpose
This PRD sketch proposes a small-scope feature set that makes customer-managed networking onboarding (VPC peering/handshake) faster while preserving a strong forensic trail for audits. The tension we want to resolve: operators need low-latency approvals for simple, low-risk handshakes, but compliance teams require immutable, queryable evidence for each step.

Problem statement
- Current private onboarding flows are slow: customers and operators report 2–5 day cycles because we require manual evidence packaging and review for every network change.
- Large customers want a "fast-path" for low-risk changes (new private route, ephemeral peering) but still need a chain of proof that satisfies auditors.
- Storing full syslogs and packet-level telemetry for every change is expensive and increases retention burden for customers.

Goals
1) Define a compact evidence schema that captures authorization, attestation, and runtime proof for a network change (compact proofs should be verifiable and append-only).
2) Implement a "fast-path" onboarding mode: automated checks + sampling telemetry that allow operator-approved changes to be applied within minutes for low-risk classes.
3) Ensure evidence is retained and queryable according to customer-configured retention tiers (short, standard, audit) with export hooks for e-discovery.
4) Provide developer-friendly APIs for customers to pull proofs or subscribe to a proof stream.

Non-goals
- We are not building full packet capture or deep packet inspection.
- We will not integrate with all KMS providers in initial launch (limit to AWS KMS + Redwood KMS).

Key concepts / definitions
- Evidence capsule: compact signed bundle describing a change request, decision, and minimal runtime telemetry (prefix hashes, handshake receipts).
- Fast-path class: a policy classification (low|medium|high) derived from heuristics and past behavior. Only low-risk classes are eligible for fast-path.
- Proof cursor: a replayable id that allows auditors to fetch the full chain for a given change.

High-level flow (happy path)
1) Customer initiates a change: request includes topology intent, CIDR, operator contact, desired retention tier.
2) Redwood pre-checks: model-based heuristics + configuration checks (no overlapping CIDR, SLA available, operator in approved roster).
3) If low-risk and customer opted-in to fast-path: automated approval is issued, change applied, evidence capsule created and stored in the append-only ledger. Operator and customer receive a short receipt.
4) Periodic sampling job (configurable rate) collects compact telemetry (KV cache digest, handshake timing, lightweight tracer spans) and attaches to the capsule.
5) For sampled events, extended telemetry is stored under the chosen retention tier and marked for potential e-discovery export.
6) For high/medium risk or when pre-checks fail: create an evidence capsule, escalate to manual review, attach reviewer notes and final verdict to the capsule.

Evidence capsule schema (compact, human-readable fields)
- capsule_id (UUID)
- requestor: principal id (string)
- customer_tenant_id
- change_type (vpc-peer | route-add | nat-rule | keystore-rotation)
- policy_class (low|med|high)
- precheck_summary (list of checks: pass/fail)
- operator_decision: auto|manual + signer id
- timestamp_request, timestamp_decision
- retention_tier (short|standard|audit)
- compact_telemetry_digest (sha256 of compressed sampler output)
- proof_signature (signed by Redwood signing key)
- proof_cursor_url (opaque id for fetching full artifacts)

Note: the schema above is intentionally compact to reduce storage and improve query speed. Full artifacts (expanded telemetry, logs, reviewer attachments) are stored separately and referenced by proof_cursor_url.

APIs and UX
- POST /v1/private/evidence/requests -> create change request (returns capsule_id + provisional status)
- GET /v1/private/evidence/{capsule_id} -> fetch capsule (compact) + links to full artifacts
- GET /v1/private/evidence/{capsule_id}/export -> request packaged export (zip with signed manifest) for e-discovery
- Web console: Onboarding -> Fast-path toggle per-customer, sampling % slider, retention tier dropdown, list of recent capsules with quick filters.

Retention tiers & pricing notes
- short (30 days): default for fast-path; capsule retained + sampling metadata. Lower cost.
- standard (1 year): default corporate tier. Full capsule + sampled telemetry stored for 1 year.
- audit (7 years): for regulated customers; full artifacts stored and immutable for 7 years. Premium price.
Pricing: offer fast-path discount (5–10%) when customers accept short retention and opt into sampling.

Sampling strategy
- Deterministic sampling for reproducibility: hash(capsule_id) % 100 < sampling_rate
- Sampling rate per customer configurable (0–100%). Default 5% for fast-path.
- Sampled artifacts: expanded tracer spans, connection handshake logs (only metadata), operator comment snapshots.

Security & compliance considerations
- Capsules are signed with Redwood operational key stored in HSM; customer-facing export can be re-signed with customer KMS (optional) for chain-of-custody.
- Append-only ledger: use time-windowed sharding + signed sequence numbers to make tampering detectable.
- PII minimization: avoid storing raw IP logs in compact capsule; only include digests and summarized metadata. Full telemetry only stored when required and flagged as "sensitive" for retention policy enforcement.
- Audit hooks: support syslog-forwarding of capsule events to customer SIEM (S3, Splunk, Datadog).

Operational runbook (rough)
- Fast-path alerts: when fast-path auto-approval rate drops below threshold or sampling shows anomalies, trigger rollback window and notify SRE/product.
- Manual review SLAs: initial ack within 1 business hour, final decision within 24 hours for medium risk. High risk per customer SLA (usually 48 hours).

Open questions / decisions needed
- Which Redwood signing key rotation cadence ensures forensic integrity without breaking export verification? (security input required)
- Export format: signed ZIP + JSON manifest vs. WARC? (legal prefers signed ZIP + canonical JSON).
- Default sampling rate — starts at 5% but needs validation via early experiments.
- Do we require explicit customer opt-in for fast-path or make it default with an easy opt-out? Risky from compliance perspective.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Evidence capsule created for every private onboarding event and queryable via API within 30s of decision.
- Fast-path auto-approval reduces mean lead time for eligible changes from days to <10 minutes for 90% of cases.
- Sampling pipeline stores expanded telemetry for at least 5% of fast-path events and those artifacts are exportable.
- Basic web UI controls for toggling fast-path and sampling are present in Console.

Rollout plan (phased)
Phase 0 (internal pilot, 2 weeks): implement capsule schema + internal-only signing, pilot with two internal customers (SE team).
Phase 1 (beta, 8 weeks): external beta with opt-in fast-path for a handful of customers; sampling default 10% for early telemetry.
Phase 2 (GA, 12+ weeks): full product with retention tiers, console controls, export APIs, pricing.

Testing & validation
- Simulated workload: replay 30 days of historical onboarding flows to validate precheck accuracy and false positives for fast-path.
- Red-team: attempt to tamper with capsule ledger to validate detection logic.
- Audit rehearsal: produce e-discovery export for a sampled customer and validate with legal.

Notes to self / TODOs
- [ ] Confirm legal preferences on export format (Priya)
- [ ] Seed pilot customers and draft onboarding email (Omar)
- [ ] Wireframe console UX and locate Console API owner (Liam)
- [ ] Implement minimal proof_cursor_url service and S3 storage pattern (infra)

Appendix: quick sketch of console copy (for UX)
- Fast-Path Onboarding: "Enable low-latency approvals for routine network changes. We’ll sample a small % of events and keep compact evidence by default. Choose a retention tier to match your compliance needs."
- Sampling tooltip: "We randomly select events for deeper telemetry collection to keep costs low while enabling audits."

End of draft.

-- nina

(Comments welcome — this is intentionally concise to iterate quickly. Link above to confluence has timeline and estimated cost model.)
